top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single idea (magic-wavelength trapping) with a clear origin in Katori's proposal and first Sr demonstration, taken to the 10^-18 regime by Ye and independently reproduced and cross-compared in several institutions. It opens measurements (relativistic geodesy, constants drift, dark-matter searches) that were not possible before, and the two-name allocation is uncontested. The caveats are overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and unchecked secondary priority claims, so the citation must be confined to the lattice clock. P002 is a genuine discovery but has a real credit gap (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and overlaps the 2016 prize, so it ranks second; an award is still preferable to no award.
